# Profile-hot guest functions, one address per line (e.g. 0x82161B40 or sub_82161B40; '#' starts a comment).
# tools/switch-direct-calls.py defines them as PPC_HOT_FUNC_IMPL: GCC optimises them harder and groups them in
# .text.hot. The first 600: from the perf4 CPU profile (2026-10-01, 9 reports, 270 s; all threads), the functions with
# the most samples among those without double-precision or vector floating-point arithmetic
# (tools/switch-codegen-pass.py's test), as in UnleashedRecomp-NX round 14: the attribute can change GCC's unrolling
# and with it its multiply-add choices, so the floating-point ones stay as they were. perf8 adds the hottest of the
# perf7 profile (2026-10-02, 17 reports, 510 s) up to 1000, among those without any floating-point product either, and
# keeps the first 600 as they were (taking the attribute away could move a multiply-add just as giving it).
# Regenerate with tools/switch-cpu-profile.py --hot-list (and the same filter). SWITCH_HOT_FUNCTIONS=0 ignores it.
